newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia regulator postpones balloting on two IPOs.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia regulator postpones balloting on two IPOs.

text.p: Malaysian capital markets regulator, the Securities Commission, said on Tuesday it was postponing the balloting of shares for two companies due to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE).

The balloting of shares in Fumakilla (Malaysia) Bhd and Trans Capital Holdings Bhd would be postponed until further notice, the commission said in a press statement. It said the postponements had been ordered for differing reasons but did not give details.

"The Securities Commission (SC) confirms that it has instructed...the issuing house concerned, to postpone the balloting of Fumakilla (Malaysia) Bhd shares," said the statement, in response to local press reports about the postponement.

The SC said it is meeting on November 28 to discuss the matter, after which it will issue a statement on the postponement of Fumakilla balloting by share-issung house MIDF Corporate Consultancy Services Sdn Bhd.

"For unconnected reasons, the SC has also asked the same issuing house to postpone the balloting of Trans Capital Bhd shares scheduled for 27 November. A further statement on this postponement will be made as soon as possible," the SC said.
Fumakilla makes household insecticides, while Trans Capital is a maker of electronic components.
